sections.html:
Yes, as long as you match the method to the house. Choices run from a regular agent listing to selling it yourself to a cash buyer, and the condition of the house, any tenants and your deadline usually decide.

This is the Town of Wallkill in Orange County, which wraps most of the way around the city of Middletown. A hamlet with the same name sits in Ulster County, so make sure each tax bill, record or listing you rely on points to the Orange County town. Your sale will touch the town Assessor, the Receiver of Taxes, the Orange County Clerk, and one of five school districts, depending on where the parcel sits.

Roughly two in three homes are owner-occupied, and the average commute is a little over half an hour.

Highway access drove the growth: 11,518 people in 1970, 20,481 in 1980 and 30,486 in 2020. Shopping gathers on Route 211, home to the Galleria at Crystal Run, and Interstate 84 crosses NY Route 17 in the south. Hamlets include Scotchtown, Circleville, Howells, Mechanicstown, Michigan Corners, Phillipsburg, Rockville and Washington Heights, and East Middletown is a village inside the southeastern part of town.

sections.h2: School districts and school tax bills
sections.html:
The town is divided among several districts. Its tax page names school tax collectors for Middletown, Pine Bush, Valley Central, Goshen and Minisink, and each sends its own bill from its own website.

Collection windows differ. Middletown collects from October through February, while Pine Bush, Valley Central, Goshen and Minisink list September and October. Know which district holds your parcel, because it fixes the school tax amount, who collects it and who provides the payoff. Buyers comparing schools start from the same point, so name the district in your listing.

sections.h2: Town and county tax due dates
sections.html:
Town and county bills go out around December 30 from the Receiver of Taxes, whose office handles over 10,000 of them. Payment runs in three stages:

  • January 1 to 31: no penalty.
  • February 1 to 28: 1 percent penalty.
  • March 1 to 31: 2 percent penalty.

Partial payments and installments are refused, and by law the office cannot accept anything after March 31. Whatever is unpaid on April 1 is returned to the Orange County Commissioner of Finance in Goshen.

Under Real Property Tax Law section 992, a missing bill does not cancel the tax or the fees that follow. Call the Receiver of Taxes if nothing has arrived by early January. Paying on time in January avoids any penalty at all.

The Assessor maintains the roll behind town, county, school, fire district and library taxes and handles exemptions: STAR Basic and Enhanced, military service, low-income senior, disability with limited income, agricultural, clergy, not-for-profit and firefighter. Applications are due March 1. Anyone who bought after 2015 registers for STAR with the state.

Disputing an assessment means filing Form RP-524, the Complaint on Real Property Assessment, between May 1 and Grievance Day, the fourth Tuesday in May. Filing sets your appointment time, and the Board of Assessment Review mails its decisions on July 1.

Owners are responsible for keeping their mailing address, escrow account and property inventory accurate with the Assessor. After closing, send over the new owner's mailing address so the next bill reaches the right person.

Wallkill deeds are recorded by the Orange County Clerk. Charges: a $45 flat fee covering the recording page, $5 for each further page, $5 for the TP-584, $10 for the state deed fraud letter, and the RP-5217 at $125 for a single-family or agricultural parcel or $250 for commercial and vacant land. Transfer tax is calculated on the total consideration and added.

Cash and checks are the only accepted payments. Personal checks above $250 are refused, and any business, attorney or title company check above $10,000 has to be certified or replaced with a money order.

  • Spell the grantor and grantee names the same way on every document.
  • Notarize the seller's signature, and sign everything in original ink.
  • The legal description on the deed should name the state, county, town and village.
  • Black ink on white paper only, with no correction fluid or tape.

The clerk's office examines documents for recording requirements but not for legal sufficiency, so have your closing attorney review the deed first.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
Pull these together before an offer arrives and you save days. The offices named above can supply each one.

  • Current town, county and school tax bills, which show the buyer the district.
  • Your STAR registration status, since owners who bought after 2015 register with the state.
  • Permits and certificates of occupancy for renovations.
  • The current deed; the Orange County Clerk can provide a copy.
  • Lease copies for any tenant who will stay past closing.

Once those are in your attorney's hands, the payoff request to the Receiver of Taxes and the TP-584 and RP-5217 can be prepared without further input from you.

If tenants will remain after closing, bring their lease copies to the attorney as well. A buyer who plans to keep them needs the terms, and a buyer who wants the house empty needs to know that early. Either way, tell the tenants about the sale before the first showing, and ask them how much notice they need. Showings go more smoothly that way.

You will find Building and Code Enforcement at Town Hall, where forms are posted, including demolition application documents for 2026. Should a previous owner have added a deck, finished a basement or built an addition, find out which permits and certificates of occupancy exist for the address before pricing the house.

Lenders and buyers' attorneys check whether what was built matches what was permitted. Any difference can slow closing or prompt a lower offer, and resolving it before listing keeps the timeline under your control.

Cash buyers need no lender appraisal or loan approval and take the house as is, so you can drop the repair list and most staging. The legal side is unchanged, because a tax payoff, a deed, transfer forms and county recording are needed in every sale.

A workable order for a Wallkill seller: identify the school district, ask the Assessor about exemptions and STAR, check permits with the Building Department, get a payoff from the Receiver of Taxes, then give the closing attorney the deed details. Doing the first three early removes most of the surprises that come up between contract and closing.

faqs.q: How quickly can I sell a house in Wallkill for cash?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close in a few weeks when title is clear. Delays usually come from estate paperwork, tenants or a missing permit, so start with those.

faqs.q: What does a typical house in Wallkill cost?
faqs.a: The middle value for owner-occupied homes is $353,200, with rent around $1,790 and 64.1 percent of homes owner-occupied.

faqs.q: When are Wallkill town taxes due?
faqs.a: January 1 to 31 without penalty, with 1 percent added in February and 2 percent in March. The Receiver of Taxes cannot accept payment after March 31.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Wallkill?
faqs.a: The fourth Tuesday in May. File the RP-524 complaint form from May 1 through that day, make an appointment, and expect the Board of Assessment Review's decision on July 1.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Orange County Clerk by credit card?
faqs.a: No. Recording payments must be cash or check, and personal checks over $250 are refused.
